question: What is the primary viral cause of severe, dehydrating diarrhea in infants and young children?
explanation: Rotavirus is well-documented globally and locally as the most common viral pathogen responsible for severe dehydration episodes in young children. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h1)

question: How does gastroenteritis fundamentally affect the gastrointestinal tract?

options.A: It blocks the bile ducts and stops liver enzyme production
options.B: It creates permanent ulcers in the lower esophageal sphincter
options.C: It permanently destroys the muscular wall of the large bowel
options.D: It causes inflammation of the stomach and intestinal lining

explanation: The core pathological feature of gastroenteritis is the acute inflammation of the mucous membranes inside the stomach and intestines. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h1)

question: What is the main route of transmission for the pathogens that cause gastroenteritis?
explanation: Gastroenteritis pathogens spread primarily when microscopic amounts of infected stool contaminate food, water, or hands and enter a new host's mouth. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h2)

question: Why does a patient with acute gastroenteritis experience watery diarrhea?

options.A: Pathogens trigger excess fluid and electrolyte secretion into the gut
options.B: Kidneys dump excess water directly into the large intestine
options.C: The stomach completely stops all digestive enzyme production
options.D: The liver stops producing bile needed to bind stool together

explanation: Toxins and cellular damage force the intestinal lining to secrete large quantities of water and salts, overwhelming the bowel's ability to absorb them. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h2)

question: Which finding is a classic sign of severe dehydration during a physical assessment?

options.A: Pounding pulse and high blood pressure
options.B: Poor skin turgor and dry mucous membranes

explanation: As the body loses water, skin loses its elasticity and the mouth and tongue become visibly dry. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h3)

question: A mother brings her toddler to the clinic with 10 episodes of watery diarrhea today. Which assessment finding requires immediate nursing action?

options.A: Mild fussiness when the mother tries to feed him
options.B: Sunken fontanelle and no wet diapers for six hours
options.C: Mild low-grade fever of 37.8 degrees Celsius
options.D: Loose stool containing small pieces of undigested food

explanation: A sunken fontanelle and lack of wet diapers indicate dangerous dehydration and reduced kidney perfusion, requiring urgent fluid resuscitation. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h3)

question: When is a stool culture typically ordered for a patient with gastroenteritis?

options.A: Only after the patient has fully recovered from illness
options.B: When symptoms are severe, persistent, or contain blood
options.C: To test if the patient's liver enzymes are elevated
options.D: For every single patient who reports mild vomiting

explanation: Routine mild viral cases clear up on their own, so cultures are reserved for severe, prolonged, or bloody presentations to identify the exact germ. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h4)

question: Why would a doctor request serum electrolyte tests for a patient with severe vomiting and diarrhea?

options.A: To check for dangerous mineral losses like sodium and potassium
options.B: To measure how fast the stomach lining is healing itself
options.C: To check if the patient has developed a food allergy
options.D: To determine the exact species of virus causing the infection

explanation: Frequent fluid loss depletes essential body salts, and blood tests help guide safe intravenous or oral electrolyte replacement. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h4)

question: What is the primary goal in the medical management of acute gastroenteritis?

options.C: Placing the patient on a strict zero-food diet
options.D: Giving strong antibiotics to kill all viruses

explanation: Preventing or correcting dehydration is the single most important intervention to save lives in gastroenteritis. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h5)

question: Why is oral rehydration salt (ORS) solution preferred over plain water for rehydration?

options.A: It tastes much sweeter so children will drink large amounts quickly
options.B: It contains strong antibiotics that kill bacteria inside the stomach
options.C: It contains a specific ratio of glucose and sodium that enhances water absorption
options.D: It numbs the stomach lining to stop painful vomiting right away

explanation: The sodium-glucose cotransport mechanism in the intestine uses glucose to pull sodium and water back into the bloodstream effectively. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h5)

question: What is the most immediate life-threatening complication of untreated, profuse watery diarrhea?

options.B: Enlargement of the liver and spleen

explanation: Losing massive amounts of body fluid without adequate replacement drops blood volume dangerously low, leading to shock and organ failure. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an effective strategy for preventing the spread of gastroenteritis in a community?

options.A: Giving rotavirus vaccines to young infants
options.C: Washing hands regularly with soap and clean water
options.D: Ensuring access to safe and treated drinking water

explanation: Daily antidiarrheal drugs do not prevent infections or transmission; hygiene, safe water, and vaccination are the true preventive measures. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h6)
